title: [MILL Senior Friday] World of Film with Mark Phelan
description:
Join us on Fridays for a day full of events for Seniors with the MILL @ MPL! All events are free and open to the public. Registration is recommended unless otherwise noted.


Ride the High Country (1962) | NR
Reduced to transporting gold from a distant mine to a small-town bank, retired lawman Steve Judd recruits friend Gil Westrum, who has been performing in a traveling carnival. Unknown to Steve, the restless Gil and a young drifter intend to steal the next gold transport. On the way, the men help Elsa Knudsen to break free from her zealot father and join her fiancé at the mine, not realizing the consequences that await them all.

ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR
MARK PHELAN - I am a lifelong film fanatic who eats, breathes, sleeps and drinks movies. I have studied with Donald Spoto at the New School in NYC and have a BA and MA in Speech and Theatre from MSU. I have also worked as an actor and have directed several plays in local regional and community theaters, including the Whole Theatre in Montclair and the Paper Mill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ. I am currently working as an adjunct professor teaching, among other courses, Introduction to Cinema.

title: Theater League of Clifton presents: The Altos!
location: Mario’s Restaurant & Pizzeria, 710 Van Houten Ave, Clifton, 07013, United States
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will present “The Altos”, an interactive dinner theater comic mystery by David Landau, for three weekends in August 2026. 
Performances will be held at The Village Inn, 422 Runnymede Dr, Wayne, NJ 07470 on:
Friday, August 14
Saturday, August 15
Sunday, August 16 
…and Mario’s Restaurant & Pizzeria, 710 Van Houten Ave, Clifton, NJ 07013, on:
Friday, August 21
Saturday, August 22
Sunday, August 23
Friday, August 28
Saturday, August 29
Sunday, August 30 
Friday and Saturday performances will begin at 8pm, with Sunday performances beginning at 4pm. 
Meet the crime family that inspired it all: the Altos! (like ‘The Sopranos’, only lower!) 
It is Tony Alto’s funeral—or is it? His wife, Toffee, has invited everyone to the wake, but almost no one seems particularly sorry that Tony is gone. When Tony unexpectedly turns up alive, his family appears
even less pleased, leaving the audience to determine who put a contract out on him. Filled with outrageous characters, family feuds, suspicious behavior and plenty of surprises, “The Altos”
invites audience members to become part of the mystery and see whether they can identify the would-be killer. 
The production is directed by Maren Sugarman and produced by John Traier. The stage manager is JoAnne MacBeth. 
The cast includes Karen Bednarz, Stephen Burke, Felipe Rodriguez, Sheldon Stone, and Collin Wehr. 
Tickets are priced at $70, which includes a dinner buffet. Tickets may be reserved at 973-928-7668, www.theaterleagueofclifton.com, or by regular mail—payment by check only. The Theater League’s
mailing address is P.O. Box 4072, Clifton, NJ 07012. 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment
for audiences of all ages. 
For additional information about “The Altos” and other upcoming productions, visit www.theaterleagueofclifton.com

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let me know by the day before. If you show up later than 9 AM and we have to rotate people in then those who show up by 9 AM will have court priority. It all depends on how many people we have vs. court space on any given day. Keep monitoring the comments for any changes though keep in mind I typically don’t monitor comments after 9 AM.

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal locked\-team matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll use a structure I learned for balanced clinic matches\. This typically includes quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages “dream\-team” scenarios trying to hold the court via wins\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Let's Walk!! Garret Mountain
description:

Join me for the 5K paved loop at Garret Mountain Reservation.
We will meet at the parking lot on the loop, turn right on Park Ave from Mountain Ave, lot is on the left. GPS Address for Garrett is 8 Mountain Ave Woodland Park.

Garret Mountain Reservation, located in both Woodland Park and Paterson, is one of Passaic County’s most frequented parks. The original landscape was designed by the famed Olmsted Brothers Firm. The 310 acres of recreational space sits more than 500 feet above sea level, with scenic views of Paterson and the New York City skyline. Lambert Castle and Lambert Tower, two of Passaic County’s historic sites, are also located within Garret Mountain Reservation.

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

Collaborative walk with "Montclair Women Over 50."

title: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg
description:
Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg
Closing Event for “Unrecyclable: Look Again” 
What do you see when you really look at what you throw away? 
Join artist Andrew Borg for the closing event of Unrecyclable: Look Again — an afternoon that begins with a gallery talk and ends with your hands deep in materials you never thought twice about discarding. 
After walking through the exhibition and sharing the story behind his two-year collection of unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites, Borg leads an immersive hands-on Assemblage Lab in which participants get to experience the process firsthand. Using unrecyclable packaging, abandoned electronics, appliances, and other “ghost objects,” you’ll build your own assemblage, sculpture, or mixed-media artwork — guided by the same impulse that drove this exhibition: look again. 
No artistic experience required. No right or wrong. Just a fresh set of eyes and a willingness to see the overlooked as raw material for something new. 
Unrecyclable materials are provided, along with glue to put your assemblages together. Bring your own materials too — packaging, foam inserts, bottle caps, old electronics, anything you’ve been meaning to throw away. The stranger the better. 
🗓 Saturday, August 22 | 1:00 pm – 3:00 pm
📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, 2nd Floor, Montclair, NJ
🎟 $10 
Part gallery talk, part art lab, all creative. Come ready to make something!

title: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk — Unrecyclable: Look Again

Materials provided; bring your own discards too, the stranger the better. No prior experience required. $10. Register in advance or at the door.

title: Food Tour and History Walk of Montclair
description:
Explore Montclair, NJ on this immersive food tour showcasing a hyperlocal culinary hotspot, co-hosted by Chow Town Food Tours and Montclair History Center. 
“Montclair In Motion” is a social, flavorful experience rooted in this colorful community’s unique industrial history and more recent cultural growth, including culinary traditions from Argentina, the Philippines, Sicily, West Africa, and Brazil. 
Chow Town Food Tours and the Montclair History Center will provide expert insights for a tour to remember. This guided exploration of Bloomfield Avenue will lead guests on a leisurely one-mile walk, stopping for Brazilian comfort food, humongous cookies, and more. Meet the chefs and business owners that make this one of the most exciting restaurant scenes in the state. 
Discover the hidden history behind architecture, landmarks, and other notable highlights from the experts at the nonprofit Montclair History Center. 
Bring an appetite! The tour will visit several fantastic NJ eateries, including unapologetic Jersey pizza, Calabrian-style; international fusion cuisine with a twist from Montclair locals; Brazilian homestyle fare from a lauded cookbook author; a slinger of humongous, addictive cookies; and more!

title: Unearthing Our Past: Revolutionary Stories
description:
Unearthing Our Past: Revolutionary Stories

Presented by West Orange Township Historian Joseph Fagan

West Orange Public Library – August 22, 2026 – 2pm

 

Join West Orange Township Historian Joseph Fagan as he unearths the many stories forgotten by time at the Old Burying Ground in nearby Orange. Here weathered gravestones and forgotten burial plots reveal the many stories of West Orange’s first settlers. Join Joseph Fagan as he steps through an undisturbed portal in time where Revolutionary War patriots, local families, and ordinary citizens still bear silent witness to history. Discover the stories of the people whose lives, sacrifices, and experiences helped shape both our local community and the nation.

 

Presented as part of the commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary, this program is the second in a series by Joseph Fagan supporting Rev250 NJ. It is a statewide initiative that explores the unique Revolutionary War history of communities across New Jersey. Join Fagan for an engaging journey into the people, events, and stories that helped define our nation and continue to shape our local heritage today.

title: Shawangunks Loop Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this interesting loop hike in the Shawangunks of New York!
For this 15 mile loop trip, we will meet at the Foordmore Trailhead for the Long Path near Kerkhonksen New York.
The most difficult parts will be the very beginning where we ascend the Shawangunk Ridge on backroads and the Stony Kill Carriageway.
Once we reach the top of the ridge, we continue a bit through the blueberry lands, and then descend a bit on Smiley Carriageway. There will be one rough bit of trail down to a waterfall, and then more pleasant back roads. There is one bit that has metal rungs to climb up, but it is quite short. I'll be prepared with a pack to carry all of Ev's stuff for this stretch.
The only regular road walk stuff is pretty much at the very beginning, and the beginning of the ascent.
Once we do the entire ridge bit, two thirds of the hike, we'll make our way onto the Delaware and Hudson Canal, as well as the O&W Rail Trail.
This will provide us with an easy creekside walk for the last stretch.
Apart from two difficult miles, the rest of the hike should be very relaxing.
The gradual climb will be on back road and dirt road, and then trail. After that, we have ten miles of gradual downhill to flat.
There are going to be a few stores in Ellenville at mile 11 or 12, but otherwise there are no other stores along the way.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let me know by the day before. If you show up later than 9 AM and we have to rotate people in then those who show up by 9 AM will have court priority. It all depends on how many people we have vs. court space on any given day. Keep monitoring the comments for any changes though keep in mind I typically don’t monitor comments after 9 AM.

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal locked\-team matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll use a structure I learned for balanced clinic matches\. This typically includes quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages “dream\-team” scenarios trying to hold the court via wins\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop
description:
Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop
What if the Tarot could speak in your voice? 
In this exploratory workshop, we’ll dive into the rich history and symbolism of the Major Arcana — exploring the colors, archetypes, and allegories that have given these iconic cards their power for centuries. Then, we’ll turn that wisdom over to your own creative instincts. 
No art experience needed. No tarot experience needed. Just an open mind and a willingness to listen to what’s stirring inside you. 
You’ll choose a card that calls to you, journal your reflections, and then bring it to life through drawing, painting, or collage — reimagining it through your own symbols, style, and personal expression. The goal isn’t perfection; it’s presence. We’re letting intuition lead. 
📅 Sunday, August 23 | 12:00 pm – 3:00 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Loft #2, Montclair, NJ 🎟 $50 | Returning participants: $30 (arrive at 1:30 pm) 
What You’ll Do: 

Explore the Major Arcana and the art of symbolic storytelling
Choose a card that resonates with you in the moment
Journal your insights and reflections
Sketch and plan your own symbolic design
Create your unique version of the card through your medium of choice.  Collage materials, magazines, paint, colored pencils and markers will be available.

All materials provided. Just bring your imagination, an open mind, a tarot deck, and a notebook. 
This is an ongoing series — each session builds on the last. Returning participants are welcome to skip the first segment and join at 1:30 pm for the creative portion only with a $30 ticket. 
  
Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. You can find her services and more at soulcentrictarot.com

title: Montclair Mixtape: Build-a-Zine with WMSC
description:
What if you could bottle up the very beginning of your Montclair story?
Montclair Mixtape is a collaborative Welcome Week zine where every student gets to create a page that captures who they are right now—their favorite songs, big goals, random interests, and everything they hope to experience during their first year at Montclair.
Then, make it yours! Decorate your page with stickers, doodles, magazine cutouts, colors, lyrics, photos, or anything else that feels like you. While creating, students can chat, swap recommendations, discover shared interests, and get to know the people around them.
Throughout Welcome Week, pages will be collected and brought together into one giant collaborative “Montclair Mixtape” zine—a snapshot of the students, dreams, personalities, and playlists that make up YOUR first week on campus.
With student permission, the finished zine can be shared digitally through Canva, creating a time capsule students can revisit long after Welcome Week is over.
Because your first week isn't just the beginning of college—it's the first page of your Montclair story. 🎧📖

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: SOLD OUT – Shorebirds with the Man Who Wrote the Book
description:
The Shorebirds workshop with Michael O’Brien has SOLD OUT. You can add your name to the waitlist by clicking on the Register Here button below.

Spend two days experiencing some of the east coast’s best shorebirding with Michael O’Brien, one of the authors of “The Shorebird Guide”! The Shorebird Guide, Houghton Mifflin’s landmark title on the subject, is authored by three Cape May birders and your guide for this workshop is one of them. Experience the best shorebirding on the East Coast with Michael O’Brien, equal parts skilled birder, expert guide and superb teacher. We’ll search South Jersey’s best shorebird locations in search of sandpipers, plovers, yellowlegs, and hope to find a few other gems such as phalaropes or godwits. Over 25 plover and sandpiper species are within reach, and some species number in the thousands here at this time of year. Begin learning identification by size, shape, behavior and voice, then move on to careful examination of plumage details, as The Shorebird Guide outlines.


We don’t pre-set an itinerary but will visit those parts of Cape May County that regularly hold good numbers of birds at this time of year. Final location decisions will be made by the leader, based on local knowledge and conditions at the time. We may walk up to 1.5 miles, over generally level, sometimes muddy or sandy terrain. This workshop may also include an indoor session, depending on weather and birds on the day. 
PREREGISTRATION REQUIRED – Ticket sales end 24hrs before the start of the event 


COST: $175 members, $225 nonmembers. 
Interested in becoming a member? Please click on the following link to learn more or join: Become a Member today! 



IMPORTANT INFORMATION: 


We bird in all weather. Be sure to check the forecast in advance and dress in layers appropriate for prevailing weather conditions. The weather in Cape May can differ considerably from nearby inland areas and may be warmer, colder, or windier so it’s best to be over prepared. We may have to bird in the rain, so please bring your rain gear. 



TRANSPORTATION: Please arrive at the appointed time with a full tank of gas, as transportation to field sites is by private vehicles.  We may walk up to 1.5 miles, over generally level, sometimes muddy or sandy terrain. Some trips involve walks over jetties. 
CANCELLATION: CMBO programs require a minimum number of registrants to run, five days in advance of the start of the tour but are seldom cancelled. If we do cancel, due to lack of participation, severe weather, or unforeseen circumstances, we notify all participants in advance, and all are eligible for a full credit or refund. Participants may cancel without penalty if greater than 30 days in advance. Cancellations 10 to 30 days in advance may be subject to a 25% service charge. No refunds or credits for cancellations less than ten days in advance unless due to health emergencies

title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and feel good. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Finding your Center Workshop
description:
Finding Your Civic Voice. Your Voice Has Power. Come learn wow to use it.
Kick off the semester by discovering the power of your voice! As part of Weeks of Welcome, Civic and Voter Engagement invites you to Finding Your Civic Voice, an interactive workshop designed to help you connect your passions with meaningful civic action.
Through engaging activities and guided discussion, you'll explore what civic voice means, reflect on the issues that matter most to you, and identify how your unique experiences and perspectives can make a difference. Whether you're passionate about education, the environment, mental health, social justice, or another cause, this workshop will help you transform your ideas into action.
Together, we'll explore how everyday actions—such as voting, volunteering, advocating, or engaging in respectful dialogue—can strengthen your community and create lasting impact. You'll also learn how to communicate your perspective in a clear and meaningful way while developing an achievable next step to stay involved throughout your time at Montclair State.
Participants will:

Explore what civic voice is and why it matters
Identify an issue they're passionate about
Develop a concise message that reflects their values and experiences
Leave with a practical action plan to begin making a difference

Whether you're new to civic engagement or already involved, this workshop is a great opportunity to meet fellow students, share ideas, and start the year with purpose. Join us during Weeks of Welcome and discover how your voice can help shape both our campus and our communities.





 











 



Hosted by: Civic & Voter Engagement, Office of Student Belonging

title: Montclair Mixtape: Build-a-Zine with WMSC
description:
What if you could bottle up the very beginning of your Montclair story?
Montclair Mixtape is a collaborative Welcome Week zine where every student gets to create a page that captures who they are right now—their favorite songs, big goals, random interests, and everything they hope to experience during their first year at Montclair.
Then, make it yours! Decorate your page with stickers, doodles, magazine cutouts, colors, lyrics, photos, or anything else that feels like you. While creating, students can chat, swap recommendations, discover shared interests, and get to know the people around them.
Throughout Welcome Week, pages will be collected and brought together into one giant collaborative “Montclair Mixtape” zine—a snapshot of the students, dreams, personalities, and playlists that make up YOUR first week on campus.
With student permission, the finished zine can be shared digitally through Canva, creating a time capsule students can revisit long after Welcome Week is over.
Because your first week isn't just the beginning of college—it's the first page of your Montclair story. 🎧📖

title: Silent Book Club Montclair
description:
At Silent Book Club® there's no assigned reading. SBC members gather in bars, cafés, bookstores, libraries, and online to read together in quiet camaraderie. All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction... it's BYOBook.


Did you love silent reading time in school? Are you more of an introvert that loves books, but doesn't want to jump into a discussion group? Are you looking to read more, but struggle to sit down and just DO IT? If you answered 'yes' to any of these, you might like Silent Book Club! Each month, we meet around Montclair and enjoy each other's company with a book of our own choosing.

Registration is required. We will be meeting at Porter Park in Montclair for all summer meetings! In the event of rain, an alternate location will be chosen.

Please be advised this book club will be meeting at a public location and therefore cannot guarantee a quiet reading environment. This book club is best for readers who enjoy a coffeeshop ambiance (low chatter, music, outside noise, etc.) or those who prefer to read with headphones.

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: POSTPONED Morning Book Club
description:
Please note: this meeting has been postponed. More information regarding a new date will be posted soon.

 

August 27 An American Marriage by Tayari Jones

Newlyweds Celestial and Roy are the embodiment of both the American Dream and the New South. He is a young executive and she is an artist on the brink of an exciting career. But as they settle into the routine of their life together, they are ripped apart by circumstances neither could have imagined. Roy is arrested and sentenced to twelve years for a crime Celestial knows he didn't commit. Though fiercely independent, Celestial finds herself bereft and unmoored, taking comfort in Andre, her childhood friend, and best man at their wedding. As Roy's time in prison passes, she is unable to hold on to the love that has been her center. After five years, Roy's conviction is suddenly overturned, and he returns to Atlanta ready to resume their life together.

title: Finding Sensitive Data Before Masking: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline
description:
Cloud Data Driven
**Presentation Title:** Finding Sensitive Data Before Masking: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Enterprise Test Data

**Abstract:**
Most data masking projects begin with a list of columns to transform. But where did that list come from? And what happens when sensitive information is hidden in fields such as notes, comments, and free-text descriptions?

This session presents a practical, human-in-the-loop pipeline for identifying sensitive columns before production data is copied into test environments. The workflow combines column-name and pattern signals, historical masking decisions, sampled values, NLP and LLM review, and final analyst approval.

Using an enterprise Test Data Management case study, I will explain how this approach reduced sensitive-data analysis time for a medium-sized schema of approximately 100 tables from about 64 hours to about 2 hours, while reaching approximately 93% agreement with parallel manual review. The session also examines false positives versus false negatives, sample minimization, responsible API use, preservation of data usability, and the reuse of approved decisions during future refresh cycles.

The session is vendor-neutral and uses only synthetic examples. Attendees will leave with an implementation blueprint they can adapt to their own data platforms and governance processes.
Available Week(s)

**Learning Objective:**
By the end of this session, attendees will be able to:
1\. Design a multi\-stage pipeline that combines metadata rules\, historical decisions\, sampled values\, NLP/LLM analysis\, and human review\.
2\. Decide which columns can be classified deterministically and which require value\-level analysis or analyst escalation\.
3\. Evaluate false positives\, false negatives\, sampling cost\, and privacy exposure when using AI for sensitive\-data discovery\.
4\. Build a reusable decision repository and feedback loop for future test\-data refresh cycles\.

title: High Altitudes and High Stakes: A Miss Marple Mystery with Lucy Foley
description:
Join us for a thrilling conversation with acclaimed author Lucy Foley as we delve into her brand-new Miss Marple mystery, Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel. 

High in the Swiss Alps, accessible only by a single, winding railway, stands the luxurious Grand Alpine Hotel. With glorious mountain views and exclusive access to powdery slopes, it draws guests from far and wide. 

The notorious actress. 

The high-flying politician. 

The society wife. 

The reckless friend. 

The shrewd doctor. 

But not everyone is here for a winter holiday. Beneath the champagne and furs, dark histories simmer; old grudges emerge like cracks in the ice. And someone is watching from the shadows. A polite, unassuming woman with an extraordinary mind: Miss Marple. When a body is found and a blizzard cuts off all escape, only Miss Marple can connect the clues before the killer strikes again. Because it isn’t a question of who has a motive, but who’s next…

Join us LIVE for a chance to win a copy of Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel! The giveaway link will be in the Resources area under the broadcast screen during the live event. Please ensure you are watching on your library's webpage for the chance to participate. 

About the Author:

Lucy Foley is a No.1 Sunday Times, Irish Times and New York Times bestselling author. More than 10 million copies of her books are in print worldwide, and several are currently being adapted for the screen. She is a Waterstones Thriller of the Month author, a three-time nominee at the British Book Awards, and The Guest List was a Reese’s Book Club selection and winner of the Goodreads Choice Award for Mystery Thriller. As a life-long Agatha Christie fan, Lucy has drawn immeasurable inspiration from the Queen of Crime. She was one of 12 writers to contribute to Marple, a collection of short stories featuring the beloved detective. And in Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel, she was inspired to transport Miss Marple – her favorite Christie creation – to the glamorous post-war setting of the Swiss Alps, in a mystery that feels gloriously escapist yet utterly relevant to our times.

title: Queer Lit Club
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This month we will be reading "Fruit Fly" by Josh Silver.

A BBC must-read book of 2026—”Sharp, dark and humorous, it’s a real nail-biter.”

Go gay. Go sad. Go dark.

A washed-up author will stop at nothing to claw her way back to relevancy—even if it means appropriating a young gay man’s tragic story.

Mallory Maddox is buried under seven years of writer’s block. With her status as a literary sensation fizzling, she’ll do anything she can to resurrect her career. Inspiration needs to strike—and fast.

Enter Leo. He’s a struggling addict sleeping under bridges and trading sex for survival. He’s vulnerable. He’s enigmatic. He’s exactly what Mallory has been looking for. 

Mallory needs Leo if she wants another bestseller. The world needs Leo’s story right now, and Mallory believes she deserves to tell it. Really, it’s her story—she’s the one who wrote it, after all. 

But as secrets threaten to unravel more than just her career, Mallory must decide how far she will go to pen the perfect story. 

A razor-sharp satirical thriller, Fruit Fly will appeal to fans of R. F. Kuang’s Yellowface and Yomi Adegoke’s The List.

title: Tarot 201: The Fool's Journey
location: Nutley - Stockton Room, Nutley Free Public Library
description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM.

No registration required! 

Are you ready for a leap of faith?!

This event is for anyone who has previously attended Tarot 101 with Kate and/or gained basic tarot skills independently. If you’re familiar with the Major and Minor Arcana and you know how to shuffle and pull the cards, then you’re ready for 201!

During our time together, Kate will explore in more depth the esoteric and spiritual principles behind the tarot, particularly the Major Arcana as seen through the lens of Jungian psychology. Taking us along the Fool’s Journey, Kate will offer card interpretations that continue to move beyond making predictions and instead focus on conscious evolution and soul growth.

Attendees are encouraged to bring a notebook and pen, plus your favorite tarot deck (if you have one). The program will begin with an extended Q&A troubleshooting session, particularly for those who have attended Tarot 101, so feel free to come prepared with questions!

While this program is designed with relative beginners in mind, more intermediate tarot learners may benefit from this in-depth review of foundational concepts.

About the presenter: Kate Sheridan, a.k.a. The Laundress, is a tarot reader and astrologer who believes that each one of us can make our own magic. Her approach is healing rather than predictive, and her work is deeply informed by Jungian psychology. You can find her on Instagram @themodernlaundress or online at thelaundresstarot.com.

title: Family History: Through Historical Research and Genealogy
description:
Information

A method that takes an investigative approach to the study of family history and genealogy. In this presentation, you will hear from a historian who has 25 years of experience doing investigations on innovative approaches to genealogy and how to think differently. There is a wide range of topics that can be covered in this course, ranging from the foundations of using Ancestry and establishing a family tree to more advanced topics such as overcoming brick walls and delving deeper into historical and genealogical material.

About the presenter


	James Calaski completed his undergraduate studies at William Paterson University of New Jersey in 1998.
	He served with the Glen Rock, New Jersey, Police Department for over twenty years, earning numerous awards and citations.
	He later earned a Master of Arts in History from William Paterson University of New Jersey in May 2013.


This program will be held in Community Room 1.

In Surviving the Lie, the final installment of this “turnpike noir” crime series, retired journalist turned private investigator Russell Avery finds himself at odds with a violent band of conspiracy theorists and ex-cops convinced that reporters are the “enemy of the people.” Face-to-face with an America where facts are more fluid than Newark’s Passaic River, he must decide if the truth is still worth fighting for. 
In addition to authoring the Russell Avery series, James Queally is a Pulitzer prize-winning criminal justice reporter for the Los Angeles Times and has covered crime and police news for the Star-Ledger in New Jersey. 
Tickets are $5 and include a 10% discount on the book purchased at the event. For more information and to purchase, visit watchungbooksellers.com.

Summer World Literature Series

THE ART OF LOSING 
by Alice Zeniter (France)
translated by Frank Wynne

Naïma's family comes from Algeria, but she knows it only from what she experiences in her grandparents' tiny apartment in Normandy: the food her grandmother cooks, the precious things they carried when they fled. Naïma's father claims to remember nothing, has made himself French. But now, one of them is going back and Naïma will see for herself what was left behind, including the family secrets. A powerful, moving family novel that spans three generations, across seventy years and two shores of the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Bowling Night - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10:15 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** Find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes and heading to the lanes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 26th bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, ping pong, skating or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

title: The Space for Words, Open Mic Night for Writers
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words – literary open-mic night hosted by the NJ Poetry Circle
August 28  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This is a monthly event on the last Friday of every month, holidays permitting. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic, and has a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let me know by the day before. If you show up later than 9 AM and we have to rotate people in then those who show up by 9 AM will have court priority. It all depends on how many people we have vs. court space on any given day. Keep monitoring the comments for any changes though keep in mind I typically don’t monitor comments after 9 AM.

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal locked\-team matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll use a structure I learned for balanced clinic matches\. This typically includes quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages “dream\-team” scenarios trying to hold the court via wins\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

description:

We're a group of people who will start by hitting the ball around for the first 20-30 minutes and then will break up into 2-4 teams for two or three hours of play.

If we have more than 20 people show up, we'll break up into three or four teams of 6 (Some may have 7, 8 or 9. Additional players just rotate into play). Games will be to 15 points. Rally scoring. Winner stays on (unless a team has won four straight).

We'll be heading outdoors to the hard court in Leonia off Overpeck County Pk Driveway in the Overpeck County Park.

\*\*\*After playing, we'll be likely heading to Tropical Juice Bar, an idea of regular attendee Kate, for a drink and snack. It's located at 60 River St. in Hackensack. Feel free to join us or suggest another spot for a post-volleyball hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play volleyball and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!!

This is a casual play. We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. Most of us are average at best, and some haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play again and hang out.

Directions: You can Google "Volleyball Court in Leonia" and it should come up. Or type 41 Willow Tree Road, Leonia, NJ 07605 into your GPS, but note that it's not on Willow Tree Road, just near it. Instead, turn onto Overpeck County Pk Driveway off Fort Lee Road (Degraw Avenue). It is past the tennis courts and near a basketball court and track. You can try Googling "Leonia High School" as well. That should help you find it. You can go to the back high school parking lot and then cross over the train tracks.

Please note. We don't have the court reserved and if it happens to be taken, we may play with those already occupying it or we will try to relocate on the fly. It's certainly possible that we may have to cancel that day if we can't find a suitable spot. And if it's looking like it'll rain or snow, I'll make a call on whether to cancel around an hour ahead of the scheduled start time.

Please bring a ball and net if you have them for possible use during the game. Feel free to bring a speaker for music, or snacks and drinks for consumption during play.

If you have trouble finding the court or group, you can call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609. There is plenty of parking and an open bathroom at the park.

title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**Saturday, August 29 4-7pm**

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation.

Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues. Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs. Sponsered by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association.

Meet at Clipper Pavilion (Not by McLoone's) on Cherry Lane in West Orange.

[Advance registration required via rahwayriver.org/calendar.html ](https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html)Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

Leader: Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway River Watershed Association (RRWA) and expert on local watershed issues.

**BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**

\# Arrival\, Weather\, & Cancellations
Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. title: Brandywine Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point 15 mile hike, the next in the Brandywine Series!
This time, we'll travel between Delacy Soccer Complex in East Bradford Township and Downingtown.
We already covered some of Downingtown previously, but this time we'll cover some other municipal trails and former route of the Brandywine Trail near the beginning, as well as the end of Struble Trail, Lions Trail, and we'll trace the historic route of the Pennsylvania Railroad New Holland Branch briefly.
From here, we take some new creekside trails, and then make our way on the Brandywine Trail up to the Philadelphia and Thorndale Branch. We take another municipal trail from here south to a pleasant back road with no lines in it, and then revisit the Harmony Hill Covered Bridge.
Along this stretch, we'll follow the alternate Brandywine Trail we saw previously, out to Sugar's Bridge.
From here, the Brandywine Trail follows a pleasant back road bit down to the Natural Land Trust Stroud Preserve.
We will hike the Stroud Preserve trails that we'd not explored before, then make our way south along Brandywine Trail to Jeffers Ford.
Another brief road walk leads us to another foot path section, then a short back road to an abandoned road which will lead us down to our end point.
The only place we pass any store on this one is in Downingtown near the beginning, so everyone should come prepared with all they need!
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let me know by the day before. If you show up later than 9 AM and we have to rotate people in then those who show up by 9 AM will have court priority. It all depends on how many people we have vs. court space on any given day. Keep monitoring the comments for any changes though keep in mind I typically don’t monitor comments after 9 AM.

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal locked\-team matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll use a structure I learned for balanced clinic matches\. This typically includes quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages “dream\-team” scenarios trying to hold the court via wins\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Long Pose Figure Drawing and Painting
description:
Tuesday Night Sessions:  Sunday Edition 
Sunday, August 30, 1 – 5 pm, $10 per hour or $35 for the full session 
“The object isn’t to make art, it’s to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri 
This special Sunday session is an extended version of our beloved Tuesday night figure drawing, giving you a full four hours to sink deep into the work. Bring your favorite materials, settle in, listen to some good tunes in great company, and get into your flow.  This will be a great opportunity to create a more finished work of art, hone your portraiture skills, or work with a material that you don’t normally get to use. 
Our model will be dressed in character (more details coming soon) and serve as our muse for the afternoon.  Whether you want to loosen up your line work, push into a sustained study, or simply spend a slow Sunday afternoon drawing from life, this is your space to do it. 
You can stay for the full session, or drop in and pay by the hour for an hour or two. 
All skill levels welcome, from seasoned studio artists to total beginners. Even poets have been known to drop in. 
Sunday, August 30 | 1:00 – 5:00 pm The Space, Montclair 
Materials such as charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paints are all welcome. Basic drawing supplies available upon request. No formal instruction is given so it is a self-guided session. 
Check out our regular weekly Tuesday night sessions here.

This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound.  The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy.  You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer.  It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. 
There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not lovers of ideas. Not lovers of comfort. Lovers magnetized by the Beloved. Those who’ve tasted the Divine Honey and cannot forget. Whose hearts remember what the mind has been taught to ignore. This is a gathering for those who feel the pull. The Assembly of Lovers meets twice each month, a rhythm of remembrance. Each gathering deepens the last. The circle becomes a living pulse of devotion. If you have a drum, bring it. Medicine drums, frame drums, and ceremony drums are all welcome. The circle grows stronger when every heartbeat joins the rhythm. 
The Flow 
Opening (5 minutes)
We set intention. A short prayer to open the way. To align the heart toward what is Real. 
Chanting and Rhythm (30-40 minutes)
Using the Sufi Chants of the Heart as a guide (our vision is for the chants to grow to what the individuals in the circle are inspired to invoke), we share simple chants. The drum holds the pulse. The voice follows. The meanings are offered, not explained. 
Repetition is the technology. The heart softens through return. Through invoking the Divine until the one invoking dissolves. 
Silent Resting (5-10 minutes)
After the chanting, we sit. No guidance. No instruction. 
The echo of the words and rhythms settles. The heart rests in what was touched. 
Closing (5 minutes)
A prayer of Unity. Of Oneness. We complete the circle and return to silence. 
Gratitude for what was offered. For what was received. 
  
Who This Is For 
This is for those who’ve felt the pull and don’t know what to call it. 
For those tired of spiritual talk that never touches the ground. 
For those who suspect that the heart knows a language the mind cannot translate. 
For those who long. 
Not for something. Not for someone. 
Just longing itself. The flame that keeps you moving toward what you cannot name but cannot forget. 
Osama Janakat 
 
Osama studied Mathematics and Physics at Rutgers University, laying a foundation of analytical thinking that complements his creative pursuits. As a beat-maker and music producer, he explores the intriguing connections between music, philosophy, and spirituality. 
Born in Jordan with Circassian roots, Osama’s move to the US in 2004 sparked a journey of inner exploration and spiritual discovery. An avid student of the Sufi tradition, he continues to seek wisdom that bridges cultures and disciplines, finding harmony in the interplay of art and spirituality.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - The Democracy We Must Keep: Why the Ideas that Built America Still Matter with David O. Stewart
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/195262

Join us as we chat with award-winning historian David O. Stewart about his newest work, The Democracy We Must Keep, and the question he explores throughout the book: What did America's founders say about democracy, and can we remain true to their vision for America?

Two hundred fifty years ago, passionate men attempted to create something the world had never seen before: a nation built not on kings or armies, but on ideas where the people ruled.

In The Democracy We Must Keep, historian David O. Stewart takes readers inside the nine key documents that shaped the formation of the United States—from Patrick Henry's thunderous cry for liberty to the carefully crafted design of a government chosen by the people, with limits on all officials holding power under the Constitution.

Through the words of seven visionary founders—Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Hamilton, Gouverneur Morris, and others—Stewart shows how a fragile experiment in self-government took shape.

These men were not saints. They argued passionately. They worried that the new nation might fall apart. Yet together, they forged the principles that must still define American democracy:


	Power must be limited.
	Leaders must answer to the people.
	Individual rights must be protected by law.


As the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary, The Democracy We Must Keep urges readers to rediscover core ideas that built the nation—and to consider what it will take to protect them.

Register today to gain a deeper understanding of how American democracy started, why it still matters, and the active role each generation must play to uphold it.

About the Author: 

David O. Stewart has published eleven award-winning and best-selling books of history and historical novels. In 2023, he received the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Washington Independent Review of Books. His most recent fictional series, the Overstreet Saga, is inspired by family stories his mother told. He lives in Maryland with the light of his life, Nancy Floreen; they have three children and six grandchildren

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and feel good. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: From Raw Data to Actionable Insights: Building Automated Analytics Workflows
description:
Cloud Data Driven
**Presentation Title:** From Raw Data to Actionable Insights: Building Automated Analytics Workflows with SQL, Power BI

**Abstract:**
Modern organizations collect vast amounts of data, but turning that data into reliable, actionable insights remains a challenge. In this session, you'll learn how to build an automated analytics workflow that transforms raw operational data into business-ready dashboards using SQL Server, Power BI, and Microsoft Fabric.

Drawing from real-world enterprise analytics experience, we'll explore practical techniques for designing scalable ETL processes, optimizing data models, automating reporting pipelines, and creating interactive dashboards that support faster, data-driven decision making.

Attendees will also learn strategies for improving report performance, maintaining data quality, and reducing manual reporting effort through automation. Whether you're building healthcare analytics, operational reporting, or enterprise BI solutions, these principles can be applied across industries.

**Learning Objective:**
Design scalable analytics workflows from raw data to reporting.
Build automated ETL and reporting pipelines using SQL Server and Microsoft Fabric.
Optimize Power BI models for performance and maintainability.
Apply practical techniques to improve data quality and reporting reliability.
Identify best practices for creating enterprise-ready analytics solutions.

title: From Her Mesa to Yours: Authentic Family-Style Cooking with Jenny Martinez
description:
Bring the vibrant, comforting flavors of an authentic Mexican kitchen straight to your home! Join us for a mouth-watering, lively conversation with viral social media star Jenny Martinez as we dive into her celebrated debut cookbook, My Mexican Mesa, Y Listo! Beautiful Flavors, Family Style. Famous for her warm personality and her signature catchphrase, "y listo and enjoy," Jenny is ready to share the multigenerational family recipes and soulful cooking techniques that have captivated millions of fans worldwide.

Jenny considers a well-fed family to be the key to a happy family. As she says, every dinner should be celebrated, and food brings people together.

My Mexican Mesa, Y Listo! features 100 recipes ranging from breakfast and appetizers to tacos, tamales, and taquitos. Jenny also covers kitchen basics for making tortillas and salsas from scratch—recipes that are sure to become staples in the home of anyone who enjoys the book. And let’s not forget her tasty desserts like churros, paletas, and Mexican bread pudding, and a few cocktails too. 

Whether you are craving crispy carnitas, comforting chiles rellenos, or sweet treats like golden churros and Mexican bread pudding, Jenny makes authentic Mexican cuisine feel approachable, joyful, and deeply rewarding.

Register today for the inspiration you need to elevate your home cooking with unforgettable food!

 

About the Author: 

Jenny Martinez is well-known across social media platforms for sharing her authentic Mexican family recipes to the delight of millions of fans on TikTok and Instagram. Jenny was born in Mexico and moved to Los Angeles at age four, yet she has never lost touch with her Mexican heritage. The traditional recipes she shares with her followers have been passed down for generations in her family. Although she later mastered her culinary arts on her own, Jenny started by learning most of her mother’s recipes at the age of thirteen. Jenny considers a well-fed family the key to a happy family and believes that dinner should be celebrated every day. Food brings people together, and Jenny’s videos and recipes convey the spirit of family and community. She lives with her family in Los Angeles, California.

description:
Start the High Holidays with joy, music and community! Join us for a lively evening packed with delicious food, soulful singing and sweet treats. office@shomrei.org

**What is Selichot?**  
The Hebrew word selichah means “forgiveness.” The plural form of the word selichah is selichot, a word traditionally used to refer to additional prayers for forgiveness recited during the month of Elul (through Yom Kippur). We gather together on the Saturday night before Rosh Hashanah to meditate on the capacity for forgiveness and on its power. In joining together, we help each other pray for that blessing – to give it and to receive it.

title: Is Your Marketing Built for Your Current Stage of Growth?
description:
Montclair Business Networking
What worked when your business was smaller may be slowing your growth now.
Growth requires change, but many companies don’t evolve their marketing strategy quickly enough.
The systems, team structure, processes, and investments that made sense at one stage can create inefficiency, inconsistent lead flow, or missed opportunities at the next stage.
So, how do you know if your marketing is where it should be?
On September 8 at 12 PM ET, join us for a virtual discussion on how marketing, sales, and operational strategies should evolve as businesses grow, and what companies at each stage should be doing differently.
What You’ll Learn

* Which marketing systems, automation tools, and infrastructure make sense at different stages of growth
* When to hire internally, outsource strategically, or keep marketing lean based on your company’s size, complexity, and growth goals
* What processes growing companies typically need to formalize to create more consistency and scalability
* How to strengthen lead generation, follow-up, sales alignment, and execution as your business becomes more complex
* The common mistakes companies make when their marketing doesn’t evolve with their growth

Who Should Attend

* Business owners and executives questioning whether their current marketing approach can support the next stage of growth
* Sales, marketing, and operations leaders responsible for driving revenue and efficiency
* Companies building, restructuring, or scaling
* Organizations looking to create more predictable growth without unnecessary overhead
