title: Everything Book Club, "Kin" by Tayari Jones
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller by the author of "An American Marriage." A selection for both Oprah's Book Club and The New York Times Book Review Book Club. 

Goes with the Open Book / Open Mind program with Tayari Jones about "Kin" the following week on Tuesday, September 15! Tickets cost $35 and include a signed copy of the book. (If for any reason you can't afford a ticket, come talk to me.)

We'll talk about Jones's conversation as well as "Kin," a poignant historical novel set in the civil rights era about two motherless childhood friends who take very different journeys: one to the storied HBCU Spellman College, the other to make her way in the world. 

TAYARI JONES is the author of four others novels, most recently the New York Times bestseller "An American Marriage," which was an Oprah’s Book Club selection and also appeared on Barack Obama’s summer reading list and his year-end roundup. It won the Women’s Prize for Fiction, the Aspen Words Literary Prize, and an NAACP Image Award and has been published in two dozen countries. Jones is the C.H. Candler Professor of English and Creative Writing at Emory University and lives in Atlanta.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Writing the Nightmare: A Ship Called Sickness and One Unforgettable Space Crew with Daniel Kraus
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/194581

Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik.

Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as “niks,” has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fém—a plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue.

The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, and—most lethal of all—a rugged, NonModded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter. The Sickness itself is mutating, possibly even pregnant. And the secret of Fém is more horrific than anyone could have imagined. To survive, Sisilla will need to forsake her predetermined fate and embrace the unknown.

Register now to gain exclusive insight from one of the most visionary voices in modern fiction.

About the Author:

Daniel Kraus is a Pulitzer Prize-winning, New York Times bestselling writer of novels, TV, and film. His novel Angel Down was the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winner, a New York Times Top 10 Book of 2025, and a national bestseller. His novel Whalefall received a front-cover review in the New York Times Book Review, won the Alex Award, was an L.A. Times Book Prize Finalist, and was a Best Book of 2023 from NPR, the New York Times, Amazon, Chicago Tribune, and more.

With Guillermo del Toro, he co-authored The Shape of Water, based on the same idea the two created for the Oscar-winning film. Also with del Toro, Kraus co-authored Trollhunters, which was adapted into the Emmy-winning Netflix series. He co-wrote The Living Dead and Pay the Piper with legendary filmmaker George A. Romero. Kraus’s The Death and Life of Zebulon Finch was named one of Entertainment Weekly‘s Top 10 Books of the Year. Kraus has won the Bram Stoker Award, Scribe Award, two Odyssey Awards (for both Rotters and Scowler), and has appeared multiple times as Library Guild selections, and more.

Kraus’s work has been translated into over 25 languages. He lives with his partner in Chicago. Visit him at danielkraus.com

title: Everything Book Club, "Kin" by Tayari Jones, Session II
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller by the author of "An American Marriage." A selection for both Oprah's Book Club and The New York Times Book Review Book Club. 

Goes with the Open Book / Open Mind program with Tayari Jones about "Kin" the following week on Tuesday, September 15! Tickets cost $35 and include a signed copy of the book. (If for any reason you can't afford a ticket, come talk to me.)

We'll talk about Jones's conversation as well as "Kin," a poignant historical novel set in the civil rights era about two motherless childhood friends who take very different journeys: one to the storied HBCU Spellman College, the other to make her way in the world. 

TAYARI JONES is the author of four others novels, most recently the New York Times bestseller "An American Marriage," which was an Oprah’s Book Club selection and also appeared on Barack Obama’s summer reading list and his year-end roundup. It won the Women’s Prize for Fiction, the Aspen Words Literary Prize, and an NAACP Image Award and has been published in two dozen countries. Jones is the C.H. Candler Professor of English and Creative Writing at Emory University and lives in Atlanta.

title: 🚶Yanticaw Park Nutley
description:
Let's Walk!!
Meet along Park Drive in Nutley near the Orechio Sports Complex. We'll walk about 3.5 mile through scenic Yanticaw Park, up to Kingsland St. and back. The path is paved and mostly flat.

Please check the event page beforehand in case of any changes. Inclement weather will cancel the walk.

The Yanticaw Park is an Essex County-owned park in Nutley, New Jersey. It is located between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, extending west to Passaic Avenue.

Essex County began purchasing land in 1911 for creation of the park. Wetlands in the park were drained, and a dam was set up to form a lake. The park was completed in 1914. In 1962, the lake, containing a small island was drained and a channel was dug as a continuation of the natural third river from the south.

PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES **EARLY** SO WE CAN START TO WALK ON TIME

Disclaimer: If you join us for a walk/hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Walk/hike will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

Our volunteers commemorate the day through meaningful service projects that foster unity, civic responsibility, leadership, and often inspire long-term community engagement.
Come join us for a day of giving back!
Volunteers will have the opportunity to choose from 20+ service sites, both on and off campus, and engage in community service projects such as:

🍎 Meal distribution and food pantry support
🌳 Park and neighborhood cleanups
🎨 Community revitalization
✨ Activities for youth, seniors, and adults with disabilities
🧼 Assembling hygiene and snack kits
 And much more!

Here’s what you can expect:

⏰ Registration at 8:00 - 8:30 AM. Event starts at 8:30 AM
🚌 Transportation provided to and from off-campus sites

title: 9/11 day of Service: Campus Blitz
description:
Honor the spirit of service on Montclair State University's Annual 9/11 Day of Service by helping ensure every eligible Red Hawk has the opportunity to make their voice heard.
Join the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement for Race to the Ballot: Campus Takeover, a campus-wide service initiative that empowers students to become civic ambassadors. During this hands-on volunteer experience, you'll learn how to confidently engage your peers in nonpartisan conversations about voting, assist them with the voter registration process, and encourage them to make a pledge to show up on Election Day.
No previous experience or political knowledge is required—just a willingness to serve your campus community and help others participate in our democracy. Our team will provide all the training, resources, and support you need to feel comfortable talking with fellow students and answering common questions about voter registration and upcoming elections.
As New Jersey's voter registration deadline approaches, volunteers will work alongside Civic and Voter Engagement staff to reach students across campus through pop-up voter registration stations and outreach efforts. Together, we'll help ensure every student has access to accurate, trusted, and nonpartisan election information.
As a volunteer, you will learn how to:

Assist students with registering to vote or updating their voter registration
Encourage fellow students to pledge to vote on Election Day
Answer common questions about voter registration and voting options
Connect students with trusted, nonpartisan election resources
Engage in respectful, nonpartisan conversations about civic participation
Help create a campus culture that values democratic engagement

By participating, you'll gain valuable leadership, communication, and outreach skills while making a meaningful impact on campus. Every conversation has the potential to inspire someone to participate in our democracy, and every new voter strengthens our community.
Whether you're passionate about civic engagement or simply looking for a meaningful way to give back on the 9/11 Day of Service, this is an opportunity to serve your fellow students while helping build a more informed, engaged, and connected campus.
No experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm, a willingness to make a difference, and a commitment to serving others. Together, we'll help every Red Hawk get election ready, one conversation at a time.

title: Blanket Making Meetup - to benefit Project Linus
location: Nutley - Stockton Room, Nutley Free Public Library
description:
All adults 18  are welcome to join us for some socializing and stitching!  We are making blankets for babies and children ages 0-18. Donations are coordinated via Project Linus, an organization that works with hospitals, shelters and agencies in North Jersey.  Please read the guidelines below carefully.

Blankets can be knit or crochet. Coffee/tea/cookies will be served.

The Guidelines:


	Please bring your own project/materials!
	Finished blankets must be new, unused, and of excellent quality.
	Yarn must be acrylic, cotton or cotton/poly blend (no wool) and washable.
	Materials must be clean, free from smoke and pet hair and other contaminants. Hospitals in particular are unable to accept blankets that are in less than pristine condition.
	Do not launder yarn, as detergents may have scents or chemicals that can’t be used around the recipients.
	Blankets will be given to children of all ages, from infant to teen, so ideal sizes would be from about 36x36 inches (newborn) and up.
	Can’t join us on the 12th? Finished blankets may be dropped off to the reference desk till the end of the day on Friday, September 25.


 

Questions?  Please call the library at 973-667-0405 ext. 2604 or email marisa.treglio@nutley.bccls.org

title: Creating a High School Roadmap - Parent & Teen Program
location: Glen Ridge - Meeting Room, Glen Ridge Free Public Library
description:
Families with students in grades 8 through 12 often arrive at junior year with very little sense of how the pieces fit together — coursework, extracurriculars, testing timelines, and applications. Until now.

In the workshop, attendees will walk away with:

       A clear picture of what each grade, 8 through 12,  should look like academically and outside the classroom

       An understanding of standardized testing timelines and how to approach them without last-minute stress

       A grounded overview of the college application and financial aid process, broken down by year

       Practical language for opening productive conversations between parents and students about goals, course selection, and next steps

Parent & Teen Program | Registration Required
OPEN to all

About the Presenter: Kevin Wallace is a licensed master social worker and co-founder of Full Circle College and Career Prep, based in Teaneck, NJ. Alongside his co-presenter, Cheryl Varghese, who holds a Master of Science in School Counseling, they work directly with high school students and families across northern New Jersey.

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.

title: (Montclair Campus) National Voter Registration Day: Race to the Ballot
description:
Join thousands of colleges, universities, nonprofits, businesses, and community organizations across the country as we celebrate National Voter Registration Day—the nation's largest single-day voter registration effort. This annual, nonpartisan initiative brings Americans together with one shared goal: helping eligible voters get registered, informed, and prepared to participate in our democracy.
Join us on September 17 from 12:00–4:00 PM in the Student Center Ballrooms and on the Quad as Montclair State University celebrates this national movement with an afternoon of civic engagement, entertainment, and community.
This year's event is proudly presented in collaboration with the Office of Commuter Life as part of Commuter Life Appreciation Week (CLAW). Together, we're celebrating the important role commuter students play in our campus community while encouraging every Red Hawk to become an informed and engaged participant in our democracy.
Whether you're registering to vote for the first time, updating your voter registration, or learning more about the upcoming election, Race to the Ballot is your one-stop destination to get election ready.
The event will kick off with welcoming remarks from Montclair State University President Dr. Jonathan Koppell, who will officially open the celebration by speaking about the importance of civic participation and the power of student voices. Throughout the afternoon, you'll also hear from special guest speakers who will share their perspectives on the importance of voting, civic leadership, and making a difference in our communities.
Enjoy a fun-filled afternoon featuring:

A giant patriotic inflatable obstacle course
Yard games and interactive activities
Free food served throughout the event
Music, giveaways, and civic swag
Voter registration assistance and nonpartisan election resources
Interactive activities hosted by campus and community partners

Be sure to stay for the entire event! Students who remain through the closing program will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win an exciting grand prize.
Together, we're joining a nationwide effort that has helped millions of Americans prepare to vote. Race to the Ballot is more than a voter registration event—it's a celebration of civic participation, community, and the belief that every voice has the power to shape the future.
The race starts here. The finish line is the ballot box. Register, get informed, and join the movement!













Hosted by: Campus Activities, Civic & Voter Engagement, Office of Commuter Life

Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12539370

title: Open Book / Open Mind, Tayari Jones; "Kin"
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
NEW VENUE! If you're going to buy the book anyway, why not see the author in conversation at the Library this fall? You can pick up your copy of the book at Watchung Booksellers the first week in March. Tickets cost $35 and include a signed copy of the book. The event will take place at the Unitarian Universalist Congregation at Montclair. Register now at tinyurl.com/OBOMTJones

Co-presented by the Montclair Alumnae Chapter of the Delta Sigma Theta Sorority. 

An instant New York Times bestseller and a selection for both Oprah's Book Club and The New York Times Book Review Book Club.

New York Times bestselling author Tayari Jones ("An American Marriage") will be talking about her Oprah's Book Club pick "Kin" with her fellow novelist and former student Cleyvis Natera ("The Grand Paloma Resort"). In the heyday of the civil rights era, two motherless childhood friends from Honeysuckle, Louisiana, find themselves taking very different paths. 

“'Kin' is the kind of all-encompassing reading experience I’m always hoping to find: smart and funny and deftly profound. This is Tayari Jones’s very best work.” —Ann Patchett



Doors open at 6 p.m. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book sales and signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. To support Open Book / Open Mind and other library programs, click here to donate.

title: Understanding Medicare
description:
Confused about Medicare? Join us for an informative session that breaks down the basics of this federal health insurance program. Learn who qualifies, including adults age 65 and older, younger individuals with disabilities, and those with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD).

We’ll explain the different parts of Medicare—Part A (hospital insurance), Part B (medical insurance), and Part D (prescription drug coverage)—and what services each covers. The program will also explore your coverage options, including Original Medicare with supplemental (Medigap) plans and Medicare Advantage (Part C).

This session is ideal for anyone approaching Medicare eligibility, caregivers, or those looking to better understand their health coverage choices.

Presented by Medicare Specialist Jacki Spear.

title: (Bloomfield Campus) National Voter Registration Day: Race to the Ballot
location: Deacon's Den and Talbott Hall Quad
description:
Join thousands of colleges, universities, nonprofits, businesses, and community organizations across the country as we celebrate National Voter Registration Day—the nation's largest single-day voter registration effort. This annual, nonpartisan initiative brings Americans together with one shared goal: helping eligible voters get registered, informed, and prepared to participate in our democracy.
Join us on September 17 from 12:00–4:00 PM in the Student Center Ballrooms and Quad as Montclair State University celebrates this national movement with an afternoon of civic engagement, entertainment, and community.
This year's event is proudly presented in collaboration with the Office of Commuter Life as part of Commuter Life Appreciation Week (CLAW). Together, we're celebrating the important role commuter students play in our campus community while encouraging every Red Hawk to become an informed and engaged participant in our democracy.
Whether you're registering to vote for the first time, updating your voter registration, or learning more about the upcoming election, Race to the Ballot is your one-stop destination to get election ready.
The event will kick off with welcoming remarks from Montclair State University President Dr. Jonathan Koppell, who will officially open the celebration by speaking about the importance of civic participation and the power of student voices. Throughout the afternoon, you'll also hear from special guest speakers who will share their perspectives on the importance of voting, civic leadership, and making a difference in our communities.
Enjoy a fun-filled afternoon featuring:

A giant patriotic inflatable obstacle course
Yard games and interactive activities
Free food served throughout the event
Music, giveaways, and civic swag
Voter registration assistance and nonpartisan election resources
Interactive activities hosted by campus and community partners

Be sure to stay for the entire event! Students who remain through the closing program will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win an exciting grand prize.
Together, we're joining a nationwide effort that has helped millions of Americans prepare to vote. Race to the Ballot is more than a voter registration event—it's a celebration of civic participation, community, and the belief that every voice has the power to shape the future.
The race starts here. The finish line is the ballot box. Register, get informed, and join the movement!

Hosted by: Civic & Voter Engagement, Campus Activities at Bloomfield, Office of Commuter Life

title: Women and Money Roundtable - How to Make Sense of Today's Financial Markets
description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: Book Talk: A Good Man by Debbie Slevin
location: Montclair Main - Classroom, Montclair Public Library
description:
Slevin delivers a riveting novel about two abused women in New York City in the wake of the 9/11 attacks… A moving novel about tragedy and recovery. -- Kirkus Reviews

Join author Debbie Slevin for a Book Talk. Her debut novel, A Good Man, explores friendship, domestic abuse, heroism, resilience, and the complicated nature of goodness in the aftermath of September 11. Her work begins with a question that refuses to let go. In journalism, nonfiction, theater, and fiction, Debbie explores the extraordinary moments hidden inside ordinary lives.

www.debbieslevin.com



Reviews
“… A powerful story with unforgettable characters, filled with compassion, humor, and hard truths…the healing power of friendship…” Alice M. Greenwald, Former President & CEO,
National September 11 Memorial & Museum.

"Debbie Slevin is a writer of extraordinary grace, wit, and feeling… inventive, daring, and brilliant on the nuances of the human heart." Hilary Leichter, author of “Terrace Story,” and "Temporary", winner of 2026 Whiting Award in Fiction.

As the story opens in 2001, journalist Elizabeth Allen drags herself up off the floor after her husband, a disgraced rock star, has brutally beaten her in their Upper West Side apartment before leaving. Across the city, Fancy Maguire showers after being raped by her fireman spouse. The 9/11 attack brings these women together after Fancy’s husband dies as a first responder at the Twin Towers and Elizabeth decides to rehabilitate her own fading career by writing about the experience of survivors. Although the two women’s circumstances are different in many ways, they find common ground in their shared despair at the hands of supposedly “good” men: “Was Frank a good man?” muses Elizabeth. “For all public accounts of his life, he was. Only Fancy and I knew the truth.” Both women struggle with their knowledge of their husbands’ violent natures. At the same time, Elizabeth and Fancy both mourn the men they once loved and think carefully about how they want the unsuspecting world to think of their spouses. Slevin structures the story around Elizabeth’s first-person narration, interspersing transcripts of her interviews with Fancy and members of her extended family and friends. Although Fancy’s experience of domestic abuse ends with her husband’s death, Slevin effectively maintains the narrative momentum with the ongoing story of Elizabeth’s traumatic marriage, which continues for a year after the attacks. Her arc notably mirrors the city’s own journey from despair to hope as she suffers a final, brutal attack, recovers, and experiences a new life as part of a larger community, including Fancy and her family. A
moving novel about tragedy and recovery. -- Kirkus Reviews

title: A.I.M by Kyle Abraham: White Space
description:
Run Time: 1 hour 
White Space brings together acclaimed composers, Jason Moran and Nico Muhly, for a haunting new collaborative score that pierces the heart of choreographer Kyle Abraham’s newest evening-length dance. At just over one hour, this dance work grounds its cast of 11 captivating dancers in a restless and thought-provoking world fueled by a vast movement vocabulary consisting of Abraham’s signature blend of classical and contemporary dance with a hip-hop underbelly. The score is performed live by two pianists on one piano, with echoes of pre-recorded hip-hop driving the collision of reality and idealism. 
“lush movement, infectious music and magnetic dancers…” (The New York Times) 
 
A.I.M by Kyle Abraham is a contemporary dance company rich with influences across genres and disciplines while remaining unmistakably its own. Described by award-winning Founder and Artistic Director Kyle Abraham as a “post-modern gumbo rooted in social dance practice,” the company produces provocative, dance-forward experiences that spotlight overlooked perspectives with depth and humanity. 
Founded in 2006 and based in New York City, A.I.M has spent two decades at the forefront of the field. It has earned recognition for its “lush movement, infectious music and magnetic dancers…” (The New York Times), becoming one of the most acclaimed touring ensembles in the world. Grounded in a commitment to reshaping how artists are supported, the company provides dancers with 52-week salaries and retirement benefits, alongside royalty payments in perpetuity for their role in the creation of new work. A.I.M continues to expand what a contemporary dance company can be and who gets to imagine themselves within it. In doing so, the organization challenges the entire arts ecosystem to create space where more people can thrive. 
For more information, to get involved, or to purchase your A.I.M merchandise, please visit http://aimbykyleabraham.org. 
Follow A.I.M on Instagram @aimbykyleabraham and
Kyle Abraham on Instagram  @kyle_abraham_original_recipe

title: Flow Into Form:  A Qi Gong and Expressive Art Experience
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Saturday September 19 | 1 – 3 pm, $40  
Breathe. Move. Create. 
Facilitated by Niraj Shah – long-time qi-gong teacher and practitioner, and Naz Botas – artist and owner of the Space. 
If you’ve been craving a gentle reset—something grounding, nourishing, and expressive—this workshop is your invitation. 
In this two-hour workshop, you’ll move through repeating cycles of Qi Gong and intuitive art-making designed to calm your nervous system, soften tension in the body, and open your creative heart. 
You’ll experience: 

Qi Gong: slow, mindful movements paired with gentle breathwork to flow your energy and bring you into the present moment
Intuitive Art: using charcoal, ink, or pastels, you’ll make marks on wall-length paper as your body moves — both naturally and through guided Qi Gong sequences — allowing your inner experience to express itself visually

Across the session, we’ll repeat several short rounds of movement followed by mark-making, gradually building comfort, curiosity, and expression. By the end, you’ll be able to look at your paper and literally see the journey your body and breath took you on. 
No prior experience in art or Qi Gong is needed. Just a willingness to breathe, move, and let the paper receive whatever wants to come through. 
Expect a peaceful, meditative atmosphere.
A safe space.
And a sense of release you’ll carry with you long after the workshop ends. 
These practices help you: 

Let go of stress stored in the body
Feel more present and grounded
Reconnect with your authentic creativity
Express yourself without pressure or judgment

A beautiful experience for anyone seeking clarity, calm, and creative freedom! 
What to Bring: 

comfortable clothing you can move in
a water bottle
an open heart and curious mind

title: NJ Code & Coffee - September meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: 7 Levels of a Web Performance Journey
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
The path to understanding the data around Web Performance, its value and business decisions surrounding this topic can be long. It is hard to see the whole journey when you and your organization are at any particular step, but it can be helpful to understand where to go next.

Eric Goldstein, Sergey Chernyshev and Alexander Chernyshev joined forces to describe and visualize this path to help make it more understandable and give you some bearings on your overall trip through various levels of this complex game.

Bios:
[Sergey Chernyshev](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sergeychernyshev/) is a web technologist with passion for web performance and open source. He is a Web Performance Engineer on the Observatory team at Cloudflare. Sergey is also Google Developer Expert in Web Technologies, specializing in Web Performance.

Eric Goldstein is a web, hardware, and infrastructure performance enthusiast. Principal Engineer at Babbel in NYC, trying to become a better open-source citizen.

**Doors open at 2pm, talk starts at 3, arrive early for networking and light refreshments.**
Bring your laptop.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Where the Paletero Man Goes: A Journey of Neighborhood, Music, and Art with Lucky Diaz (English)
description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/197986

Grab a pocketful of change and get ready to dance down the street! Join us for an energetic conversation as we celebrate the joy of community and summer fun with Latin GRAMMY-winning musician Lucky Diaz, author of the sensational bilingual picture book, Paletero Man. 

What’s the best way to cool off on a hot summer day? Run quick and find Paletero José!

Follow along with our narrator as he passes through his busy neighborhood in search of the Paletero Man. But when he finally catches up with him, our narrator’s pockets are empty. Oh no! What happened to his dinero? It will take the help of the entire community to get the tasty treat now.

Inspired by the vibrant rhythms of Los Angeles and Diaz’s own hit song, this beautiful story invites readers into a sun-drenched neighborhood where the ring of a bell means the best treat of the day is just around the corner.

Register today and discover how we can all bring a little more sweetness and community spirit into our daily lives!

Please note that we will be hosting Lucky Diaz twice on this date, once in Spanish and in English. Be sure that you are registering for your preferred format.

About the Author:

Lucky Diaz is a GRAMMY Award-winning, multi–Latin GRAMMY Award-winning artist, acclaimed author, and a leading voice in contemporary children’s literature. A six-time Emmy-nominated songwriter and Berklee College of Music alumnus, Diaz made history as the first North American children’s artist to win a Latin GRAMMY. His work bridges music and storytelling, creating a distinct body of bilingual work rooted in the cultural life of Mexican American communities in Los Angeles.

As an author, Diaz has earned some of the highest honors in publishing. His books have received starred reviews from Kirkus Reviews, School Library Journal, Publishers Weekly, and Booklist, placing him among a rare group of creators recognized across every major literary journal. His breakout title Paletero Man received a Kirkus star and audiobook distinction and was awarded the 2024 Alma Flor Ada Award for its lasting contribution to Latino-centered storytelling. He is also a recipient of the Parent’s Choice Gold Award and a NAPPA Award, further recognizing his impact on family audiences.

His latest book, Fix-It Familia, continues to build national recognition, with a Spanish edition arriving this summer, expanding access to bilingual readers and classrooms across the country.

Diaz’s work has been featured and praised by NPR, Billboard, The New York Times, and People Magazine, positioning him as a trusted creative voice at the intersection of culture, music, and literature.

Through his books, recordings, and performances with Lucky Diaz and the Family Jam Band, Diaz continues to expand the possibilities of American storytelling. He is not only contributing to the field. He is helping define it.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Paletero Man: un viaje por el barrio, la música y el arte con Lucky Diaz (Español)
description:
Debes registrarte aquí para asistir: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/198667

La duración de este evento será de 30 minutos.

Agarra un puñado de monedas y prepárate para bailar por la calle. Únete a nosotros para una enérgica conversación mientras celebramos la alegría de la comunidad y la diversión del verano con Lucky Diaz, músico ganador del premio Latin GRAMMY y autor del sensacional libro ilustrado bilingüe, Paletero Man.

¿Cuál es la mejor manera de refrescarse en un caluroso día de verano? ¡Corre rápido y encuentra al Paletero José!

Sigue a nuestro narrador mientras recorre su ajetreado vecindario en busca del Paletero Man. Pero cuando finalmente lo alcanza, los bolsillos de nuestro narrador están vacíos. ¡Oh no! ¿Qué pasó con su dinero? Se necesitará la ayuda de toda la comunidad para conseguir la sabrosa golosina ahora.

Inspirada en los vibrantes ritmos de Los Ángeles y la exitosa canción de Diaz, esta hermosa historia invita a los lectores a un vecindario bañado por el sol donde el sonido de una campana significa que la mejor golosina del día está a la vuelta de la esquina.

¡Regístrate hoy y descubre cómo todos podemos aportar un poco más de dulzura y espíritu comunitario a nuestra vida diaria!

Ten en cuenta que presentaremos a Lucky Diaz dos veces en esta fecha, una en español y otra en inglés. Asegúrate de registrarte para el formato que prefieras.

Acerca del autor:

Lucky Diaz es un artista ganador del premio GRAMMY, multi-ganador del premio Latin GRAMMY, aclamado autor y una voz líder en la literatura infantil contemporánea. Compositor nominado seis veces al premio Emmy y ex alumno de Berklee College of Music, Diaz hizo historia como el primer artista infantil norteamericano en ganar un Latin GRAMMY. Su trabajo une música y narración, creando un cuerpo distintivo de trabajo bilingüe arraigado en la vida cultural de las comunidades mexicano-americanas en Los Ángeles.

Como autor, Diaz ha obtenido algunos de los más altos honores en el mundo editorial. Sus libros han recibido reseñas destacadas de Kirkus Reviews, School Library Journal, Publishers Weekly y Booklist, lo que lo sitúa entre un raro grupo de creadores reconocidos en todas las principales publicaciones literarias. Su título revelación Paletero Man recibió una estrella de Kirkus y una distinción de audiolibro y fue galardonado con el Premio Alma Flor Ada 2024 por su contribución duradera a la narración centrada en los latinos. También ha recibido el Parent’s Choice Gold Award y un NAPPA Award, lo que reconoce aún más su impacto en el público familiar.

Su último libro, Fix-It Familia, sigue generando reconocimiento nacional, con una edición en español que llegará este verano, ampliando el acceso a lectores bilingües y aulas en todo el país.

El trabajo de Diaz ha sido presentado y elogiado por NPR, Billboard, The New York Times y People Magazine, lo que lo posiciona como una voz creativa confiable en la intersección de la cultura, la música y la literatura.

A través de sus libros, grabaciones y presentaciones con Lucky Diaz and the Family Jam Band, Diaz continúa ampliando las posibilidades de la narración estadounidense. No solo está contribuyendo al campo. Está ayudando a definirlo.

title: The Space for Words - Open mic night for wordsmiths
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words – literary open-mic night hosted by the NJ Poetry Circle
September 25  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This is a monthly event on the last Friday of every month, holidays permitting. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic, and has a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: [Outside Org]  Aging in Montclair Saturday Social
Afternoon Tea & Dessert Pairing
description:
We invite you to join us for a special Chinese tea and traditional music event. In this one-hour presentation, we will learn about Chinese gongfu tea, its cultural significance and mythical origins, taste three single-origin teas (green, white, and oolong), and conclude with a guzheng performance. 

Chinese gongfu tea is a method of brewing tea with time and effort, allowing us to control the time, temperature, and quantity of the brew to maximize the tea’s flavor. It encourages us to slow down a moment in our day, to focus on what’s in the cup, and appreciate what nature can create. Registration is required. 


Marjorie Wang grew up in NJ, and attended university in Shanghai, where she fell in love with Chinese teas. After an apprenticeship at NYC's Tea Drunk, she began sharing her passion with local communities through tea tasting events at libraries, community centers, and clubs. She has been playing the guzheng since age 12, and continues to perform at local cultural events.

title: Sonic Healing Experience with Taylor Grant
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Sonic Sound Healing Experience with Taylor Grant
Saturday, September 26 · 7:00 – 8:30 PM 
Join us for a sonic healing journey with local DJ Taylor Grant, who blends crystal bowls with intentionally chosen tracks to restore the body to resonance. Picture the lights dimmed low, the room falling away, and nothing left but sound — waves of tone rippling across your skin, low frequencies humming in your chest, crystal bowls ringing out long after they’ve been struck. Taylor curates sound journeys of all kinds, and this one is designed to let you fully rest: a ride through nostalgia, exploration, and fantasia, carried by tone and texture rather than words. 
We’re timing this with the full moon, harnessing that energy as part of the experience. In sound healing traditions, the full moon marks the peak of the lunar cycle — the moment everything you’ve been carrying rises to the surface and is ready to be released. It’s a night for letting go of what’s grown stagnant, for clarity to surface, for whatever you’ve been holding onto to finally move. The bowls and tones do the work of loosening it; the moon does the work of amplifying it. 
You’ll spend the evening lying on the floor, eyes closed, letting the sound wash over and through you — no tension, no talking, just full-body immersion in the wave, released a little further with every tone. 
Come with an open mind. Bring a yoga mat (or something soft to lie on) and a water bottle to stay hydrated — sound baths can pull you deep, and you’ll want to come back out nourished. Beyond that, you have nowhere else to be but to be! 
Please arrive before 7, and give yourself enough time to park.

title: Celebrate the publication Shibu's New Friend with author Tess Thomas (recommended for ages 4-8)
location: Montclair Main - Green Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join author Tess Thomas for a special storytime at the Montclair Public Library! Tess will read her debut picture book, SHIBU'S TAIL, as well as her brand-new sequel, SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND. The books follow the adventures of a cat named Shibu, who has big feelings and an even bigger tail. SHIBU'S TAIL has earned four starred reviews, multiple best-of-year lists, and has been published in over 18 different countries. Following the readings, Tess will answer questions from the audience and lead young readers in a Shibu and Dottie-themed craft. Copies of SHIBU'S TAIL and SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND will be available for purchase and signing following the event.

Registration is recommended but not required.

 



Tess Thomas is a writer living in Hoboken, New Jersey. She started her storytelling career at the age of four, when she would dictate tales about her imaginary friends, Sami the cat and Doodie the dog, and send them to her grandparents. Her first book, SHIBU'S TAIL, earned four starred reviews, multiple best-of-year lists, and has been published in over a dozen different languages. Tess’ favorite part of being an author is visiting schools, libraries, and bookstores to connect with young readers. She loves french fries, her kids, and her husband (sometimes in that order).

SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND

Shibu and Dottie are as different as cats and dogs — but maybe they have more in common than they think in this charming sequel to the international hit SHIBU'S TAIL!

Shibu has a lot of friends and they have a lot in common. It’s a lot of fun! But then comes … Dottie. Dottie is a DOG and she does things a bit differently. She barks instead of purrs. She tears up boxes instead of sitting inside them. She spends a lot of time … digging?

Shibu isn’t sure about a new friend, especially one so different, but he can’t help feeling like Dottie’s love for life is a lot like his own. Could this new friend actually become his best pal? Published by Levine Querido, SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND hits shelves on September 1, 2026!

title: Courage, Choice, and What Comes Next with Dystopian Icon Veronica Roth
description:
A single choice can transform your destiny. Join us for an online conversation with #1 New York Times bestselling author Veronica Roth as we celebrate the enduring legacy of her Divergent series, one of the most iconic young adult series of a generation, and get an exclusive sneak peek into her highly anticipated upcoming novel, The Sixth Faction!

Fifteen years after readers first stepped into dystopian Chicago alongside Tris Prior, the Divergent universe continues to captivate readers with its unflinching exploration of identity, courage, and sacrifice. And in the alternate universe of The Sixth Faction, we revisit familiar characters in a completely new way… 

Beatrice Prior stands on the brink of a decision every person in her world must make: five factions, five futures, five lives.

She has a plan: she’s going to make the bravest choice and leave Abnegation to join Dauntless, even though it means abandoning her family.

But when tragedy strikes at her choosing ceremony, everything changes—her world, her plans, even Beatrice herself.

Her decision will thrust her into the crosshairs of an underground rebellion, where a boy with secrets as dangerous as her own—a boy with only a number for a name—may be the only person she can trust.

One choice will change everything.

Register now for the chance to ask questions and get an exclusive sneak peek of The Sixth Faction–out on October 6, 2026!

 

About the Author: 

Veronica Roth is the #1 New York Times best-selling author of numerous titles including When Among Crows, Chosen Ones, the Divergent series, Carve the Mark and the upcoming Seek the Traitor’s Son. Veronica lives with her husband and their dog in Chicago, a city that she lovingly features (and frequently destroys) in many of her novels.

title: LINES TO LOVE: Screen-Free Afternoon with Your Child
location: The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, loft #2, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Lines to Love:  A Creative Space for You & Your Child.
Led by Leo A. Sante
Remember what it felt like to simply be together with the child you love?

No screens, no rush, no expectations.

Just being side by side, doodling, making up stories, letting your imaginations wander wherever they wanted to go. 
Lines to Love brings you back to that space. 
Using a simple roll of paper and a few drawing materials, you and your child will be guided into a playful world of co-creation. 
Together, you’ll follow lines, add to each other’s doodles, build whimsical stories, and let the drawing become a pathway to imagination. 
Lines to Love is inspired by a cherished ritual between a father, Leo, and his young son, Lucas.  Back when Lucas was little, Leo would just roll out paper and two pens. Together they’d spend hours just doodling, creating, and enjoying the precious time together. Both Leo and Lucas cherish those drawings and those moments to this day. 
This is a free flowing togetherness workshop. It’s a rare chance to share precious, screen-free time. To explore, wonder, laugh, doodle quietly. To create something beautiful side by side. 
No artistic skills necessary. Just bring your open hearts.
All materials will be provided. 
You’ll leave with unforgettable memories and a creation you’ll both cherish all your lives. 

Ticket is for an adult + 1 child. The event is structured for 1:1 time.
Additional members of a family are welcome
Each child should be joined by an adult.
All materials will be provided.
All phones will be off and set aside for the duration of the session.
Space is limited to 15 pairs, so we recommend you reserve early.

title: Everything Book Club, "The Ministry of Time" by Kaliene Bradley
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller. In the near future, a new government ministry is exploring time travel. Our heroine gets a highly paid job assisting and monitoring the time travel expat known as “1847” or Commander Graham Gore. As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.”  This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.

"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . .  A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . .  with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

Kaliane Bradley is a British-Cambodian writer and editor based in London. Her short fiction has appeared in Somesuch Stories, The Willowherb Review, Electric Literature, Catapult, and Extra Teeth, among others. She was the winner of the 2022 Harper’s Bazaar Short Story Prize and the 2022 V.S. Pritchett Short Story Prize.

Join Dee Pentyala, Ayurvedic Health Counselor and Wellness Practitioner, for an immersive, hands-on workshop where you’ll have an honest conversation about your hormones-like estrogen, progesterone, cortisol, and thyroid-in plain, everyday language. title: Pasta with a Twist: A Fresh Take on Italian Classics with Food Network Star Joe Sasto
description:
It’s time to ditch the same boring recipes and bring big, playful creativity back into your kitchen! Join us for an online conversation with Top Chef finalist and Food Network star Joe Sasto as we explore his hit national bestselling cookbook, Breaking the Rules: A Fresh Take on Italian Classics. 

Whether you are a novice cook looking to build your kitchen confidence or an experienced chef eager to expand your culinary repertoire, Joe’s approachable philosophy will change how you view everyday ingredients. We will dive deep into his vibrant world of handcrafted pasta, step-by-step rolling techniques, and unexpected flavor profiles. 

From foundational family favorites like his mom’s red sauce to daring, crave-worthy creations like Corn Cacio e Pepe, Marinated Tomato “Amatriciana,” and Pesto Pinwheel Pull-Apart Bread, this conversation is an open invitation to trust your culinary instincts and cook with absolute freedom.

Register today and learn how to make cooking fun again!

 

About the Author: 

Celebrity chef Joe Sasto found his love for cooking and appetite for Italian classics as a child at his mother's side. When the COVID-19 pandemic hit in March 2020, he pivoted his career by teaching virtual pasta-making classes.

With more than half a billion likes and countless viral social media videos, Sasto has become a recurring judge and chef personality across multiple shows on the Food Network. He's also competed and appeared on Food Network shows such as Guy Fieri's Tournament of Champions, Guy's Grocery Games, and Chopped, as well as Bravo's Top Chef and Top Chef All-stars.

In 2022, Sasto made the Food Network's first-ever "Hot List." Aside from his career as a chef, Sasto has developed a high-end customizable pasta and pizza tool line, and he is the creator of Tantos, the first puffed pasta chip, and a gourmet frozen ravioli brand, Ripi. His first cookbook, Breaking the Rules – a fresh take on Italian classics, was published in October 2025. He lives in Chicago and enjoys spending time with his pup, Tito, and his wife, Kait.

title: Breaking the Silence: Understanding Depression, Suicide, and the Power of Connection
description:
Presentation by Dr. Jason Dean and Dr. Rae Dumont

Depression is often misunderstood, accompanied with shame, secrecy or blame. So is suicide. The impact a loss by suicide has on friends and family is enormous. Without open conversations, people often feel alone as they carry the memory and question themselves about what they might have done to help. 

This presentation, in the context of a rising incidence of depression, anxiety and suicide, aims to offer understanding and compassion for people who struggle with mental illness. It  offers insights and comfort to those who have loved a person with depression, and tried to help. 

 

There will be ample time for discussion and for questions.

 

Rae Dumont, MD, LMFT, is both a pediatrician and a family therapist. While she practiced and taught at Harvard Medical School, she focused on the impact of one person's illness through the entire family, and on the interconnection between mental and physical health. 

In her family therapy practice, she helped people navigate difficulties by collaborating, rather than becoming divided. 

She is also a mother, a widow, and a friend to many. She now turns her experiences into words that speak of resilience, and the flawed road toward becoming good enough. In her fiction, she finds a personal, intimate voice, which connects emotionally with her readers’ humanity.

In the Shadow of Silence, (2-17-2026) is a novel about love, family life, and depression. She hopes for it to bring insight and comfort to her readers. 

 

Jason Dean, MD is a child and adult psychiatrist and founder of The Center for Developmental Psychiatry, a group practice in Teaneck, NJ. He is also a Clinical Instructor at Yale School of Medicine.

In his clinical work, he has worked to integrate a biological, medical view of psychiatry with a psychological perspective. Dr. Dean hopes to augment the discussion with insight gained from his clinical experience and training, as well as his work with families of individuals struggling with depression.

title: Art in Flight: Reinventing Postmodernism with Smithsonian Curator Carolyn Russo
description:
Join us for a captivating online conversation with acclaimed author and Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo as we dive into her fascinating book, The Ascent of Rauschenberg. Explore the towering legacy, unexpected inspirations, and creative heights of one of America's most influential artistic icons.

Most famous for his groundbreaking "Combines"—painting and sculpture hybrids that often incorporated everyday objects—American artist Robert Rauschenberg (1925-2008) created within a range of mediums, including collage, performance, photography, and printmaking. But a connective tissue through it all was his fascination with flight. The Ascent of Rauschenberg explores the flight motif across his work, spanning birds, insects, aviation, spaceflight, sensory experiences, and metaphors for his own life.

More than 150 images reveal the vibrant scope of his work, from lithographs inspired by the Apollo 11 launch that NASA invited him to witness and document, to a Combine featuring a taxidermied eagle that evokes Roman mythology. Nine accompanying essays reflect on his many flight themes and subtleties that might otherwise be overlooked. The book also includes archival photographs and personal papers from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation.

Register now for the chance to view art history through the unique prism of flight. 

About the Author:

Carolyn Russo is curator of the art collection at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. She has lectured internationally on the subject of art and flight and is the author of several publications including The Ascent of Rauschenberg: Reinventing the Art of Flight, Art of the Airport Tower, In Plane View: Abstractions of Flight, and Women and Flight: Portraits of Contemporary Women Pilots.

title: James Maddock
location: Outpost In The Burbs, 40 S Fullerton Ave, Montclair, NJ
description: James Maddock James Maddock’s status as a fixture on the Folk and Americana scene is confirmed with every listen of any song in his prodigious catalog. Relix Magazine put it this way: “James Maddock possesses the kind of lived-in craggy voice that would sound authoritative if he were singing the sports pages. Fortunately, he doesn't need to do that because his compositional skills are a match for his delivery." After fronting the Columbia Records band Wood, whose debut Songs From Stamford Hill was featured prominently on TV shows such as “Dawson’s Creek,” Maddock moved from England to New York City in 2003. His 2009 album Sunrise On Avenue C won a New York Music Award for Best Americana Album, while the follow-up Wake Up And Dream ranked among the top albums of 2011 in WFUV's (NYC) Listener Poll. With the release of Another Life (2013) and The Green (2015) Maddock continued to demonstrate why many consider him to be one of the best singer/songwriters working today. He has performed with Bruce Springsteen, Willie Nile, Aaron Comess (Spin Doctors) and David Immergluck (Counting Crows). According to radio legend Vin Scelsa, Maddock's "heartbreakingly beautiful and exquisitely crafted" music "touches the soul." As a songwriter, James recently had three songs co-written with Mike Scott on the new Waterboys album Modern Blues (which appeared in the Top 50 on the UKAlbums Chart), a co-write with Gary Barlow (“Actress”) on Barlow’s new album (2X Platinum), as well as a cut (“Fragile”) on the Dirt On My Tongue album by emerging UK artist Jo Harman. Songs from Another Life have been featured on NBC’s Parenthood and ABC Family’s Switched at Birth. Maddock is a constant live presence in the U.S. and in Europe. He recently completed a 25 show run with Counting Crows in the UK and Europe. Maddock’s latest release Forever June on the Master disk label is out now where music is consumed Policy For All Shows: All sales are final -- there are no refunds. Doors open 30 minutes before the show, which begins promptly at 7:30pm. By visiting Outpost In The Burbs patrons voluntarily assume all risks related to exposure to any infectious disease, including but not limited to COVID-19. Masks are not required, but always encouraged. The Outpost reserves the right to change policies at any time. Please refer to this show-specific event page or Outpostintheburbs.org for any changes.

title: Memory Café - A Dementia-Friendly Social Gathering
description:
For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.


A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.

The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.

The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.

This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.

Attendance is free but registration is required. Questions? Call 973-744-3278.

title: Crane's Mill:  The Story Behind the Name
location: West Caldwell - Community Meeting Room, West Caldwell Public Library
description:
Join local historian Bob Williams on Tuesday, October 13 at 6:30 p.m. at the West Caldwell Public Library for a fascinating look at the history of Crane’s Mill and its connection to West Caldwell.

The story has a personal connection for Williams. When he was just 15 years old, he purchased a collection of historic ledgers from Crane’s Sawmill in West Caldwell. By then, the mill had already been dismantled and moved to Allaire Village in South Jersey for reconstruction although it was never rebuilt. The mill’s foundation ruins remained in West Caldwell for years, becoming a favorite place for Williams to explore throughout his youth and into adulthood.

description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Best practices, connectivity, cross-pollination and successes are also reported. The CoM also provides assistance evaluating our ministries periodically at the discretion of the Board. title: Compagnie Hervé KOUBI: Sol Invictus
description:
Run Time: 75 minutes, no intermission. 
A jubilant ritual full of love and light from the acclaimed French-Algerian ensemble Compagnie Hervé KOUBI. Named after the “invincible sun” deity, Sol Invictus upholds love as the guarantor of peace, that despite fracture, communion emerges as humanity’s saving grace. A vivid celebration of solidarity and the bonds that unite us, in Sol Invictus the sun will emerge victorious. The score includes a composition by Swedish composer Mikael Karlsson, with excerpts by Steve Reich and digital composer Maxime Bodson. 
“The dancers of Compagnie Hervé KOUBI could be mistaken for gods.” (The New Yorker) 
About Compagnie Hervé KOUBI: Absolutely unique and utterly original, this fearless, powerful company reigns from France, Algeria, and beyond. Combining contemporary and urban dance movements, capoeira, and martial arts with powerful imagery and inspired choreography, the dancers defy gravity.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - Newark Tech Week edition
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus during Newark Tech Week!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

* your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,
* What you can help others with,
* What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

description: On Sunday, October 18, we kick off our Stewardship Campaign. This is the time of year when we each recommit our time, talent, and treasure to the Holy Spirit Verona Community. This year’s theme "Plenty Good Room" is an opportunity to be reminded that there are "many rooms" in God's house, as the Gospel Writer of John tells us. How are you welcoming others to Holy Spirit Verona? There is ALWAYS room at the table. Here is a recent Stewardship Reflection Insert for you to review.Please consider NOW how you'll support the work of Holy Spirit Verona next year with your time, talent, treasure. Can you pledge more, pledge the same or consider adding a ministry to your experience. Forms will become available in September. On Pentecost, the disciples discovered that there is no limit to God’s generosity. title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Affordable College Solutions NOW ON ZOOM
description:
Register HERE

Join us for the special ZOOM presentation of the "Cracking the Code: Affordable College Solutions" seminar.  

It doesn't matter how old your kids are...now is the time to learn how to finance college!

This program will be presented by a nationally recognized Certified College Funding Specialist who has
been invited to speak to families and professionals by more than 65 organizations nationwide. She has also
provided continuing education to over 40,000 CPAs across the country on strategies to help make college
more affordable.
Designed for parents with children of all ages—from newborn through college—this engaging and informative
session addresses one of the most stressful financial challenges families face today: how to pay for college
without jeopardizing long-term financial goals and retirement. Even higher-income families with substantial
resources can feel overwhelmed by the tremendous cost of school and seek guidance to navigate the quickly
evolving college process to secure discounts and preserve their wealth.
A featured focus of the presentation is recent legislation often referred to as “The Big Beautiful Bill,” and
what it means for college savings, financial aid, and affordability. The presenter will explain these changes in a
clear, practical, and easy-to-understand way.
Participants will also learn about:
● How to secure a quality education without overpaying for college
● Understanding the financial aid landscape: FAFSA and CSS Profiles, need-based and merit-based aid,
athletic and private scholarships
● Student Aid Index (SAI): How it’s calculated and directly impacts your family’s financial aid eligibility
● Pros and Cons of Diverse College Savings Vehicles - a look at 529 plans as well as alternative savings
strategies and determining how to choose what’s right for your family
● How to reduce student loan debt and plan for repayment without sacrificing your family’s future
● Strategies to recapture out-of-pocket college expenses
● Positioning families to maximize college discounts: Practical strategies—even for higher-income
households—to unlock savings opportunities
Participants will gain valuable insights, expert guidance, and creative strategies to help make smarter college
funding decisions while protecting the ability to retire comfortably. This program is designed to simplify and
demystify the college funding process, empowering families to reduce costs and avoid unnecessary debt.
Whether your child was just born or is approaching college decisions, this program will provide clarity,
confidence, and practical guidance you can use right away.



PRESENTED BY: Jodi Bloom, MBA
Certified College Funding Specialist
Founder and College Planning Expert

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).
